title: The known KIC 8027456 dip has a longer egress in 24 local Kepler DR25 fits
abstract: We tested the shape of the known dip of KIC 8027456 near BKJD 1448.9. We used public Kepler release 25 quarter 15 aperture and corrected flux. Split Gaussian fits give an exit-to-entry width ratio of 2.06 to 2.43 across 24 local baseline and quality choices. For two main five-day fits, all six conditional residual-block intervals stay above one. The lowest lower endpoint is 1.19. Symmetric null tail fractions are 0.005 to 0.010 with 199 samples per test. These are shape tests for a known event, not survey false-alarm probabilities. The result agrees with the prior dust-tail interpretation, but does not identify a physical cause. Both products use the same observations. Time-dependent noise, detector errors, and blended sources remain possible. We report no new event, planet, comet, or independent confirmation. The package contains the exact input, source URL and hash, code, all sample results, figures, and reproduction instructions.

display.caption: The known dip in aperture and corrected flux with split and symmetric Gaussian fits. The same split baseline is removed from both curves for display. Residuals are shown at right.
The exit-to-entry width ratio stays above two in 24 tested local fits. These fits share data and are not independent confirmations.
